theorem actual_conditional_block_product {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (O : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
        (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
      fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
        WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
    (multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (blockPrecision κ O)⁻¹).map split =
      (Measure.pi (fun j => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ (O j))⁻¹)).prod
          (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))))

atoms.text_with_tex_math: Although low query budget algorithm cannot detect the determinant sign, the norm of a target sample carries information about it. Comparing the expectations of the radial test function $x\mapsto e^{-\lambda\|x\|^{2}}$ under the two single-block mixtures gives $\mathrm{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})\geq\frac{1}{2}e^{-5n/\sqrt{\kappa}}$. A sample from the full target consists of $k$ blocks that are independent given the common sign, and tensorization of the Hellinger affinity amplifies the single-block separation to the bound below. Adding blocks does not help the algorithm, since a single query already acts on all blocks and Lemma 3.2 holds for every $k$. We summarize this property in Lemma 3.3, whose proof is given in Section B.2.
